observed_original_abi.convention_basis: PLACEMENT, NOT OBSERVATION. The body never reads ECX -- the machine-derived ABI record's inference R2 is 'ECX is never read in any form, so there is no register receiver' -- so the body is byte-identical under __cdecl, __stdcall, __thiscall and __fastcall, and the same record reached verdict ABI_UNKNOWN and abstained with reason 'no_discriminator: no stack-argument read and no positive receiver evidence'. The persisted record nonetheless asserts __thiscall with a hidden receiver in ECX, and that assertion rests on one fact: 0x00980510 occupies a word in a dispatch-table image (the sole reference in the whole program is the DATA word 0x014440e4 = 0x014440d0 + 0x14), and an MSVC x86-32 virtual member receives its receiver in ECX. This package models the receiver for arity and flags the inference rather than presenting it as a reading of the body.
observed_original_abi.ghidra_convention_note: Ghidra reports WARNING: Unknown calling convention, ghidra_calling_convention = null, ghidra_calling_convention_signal = no_information, parameter_count = 1 with the parameter in Stack[0x4]:4. The decompiler's ILayoutElement * parameter type is not independently confirmed (no MSVC RTTI in this binary; the base type arrives from imported Spore-ModAPI symbols), so the model keeps the receiver opaque rather than adopting it.
observed_original_abi.dispatch: the machine dispatch record counts indirect_calls = 0, call_offsets = [] and vtable_shaped_loads = 0, which agrees with a listing containing no transfer at all
observed_original_abi.evidence_level: ABI_INFERRED (persisted record: SUPPORTED/CONFIRMED; derived record: ABI_UNKNOWN, abstained)

mechanics.body_shape: one full-width 32-bit immediate into the return register, then the function's single exit. No prologue, no epilogue, no saved register, no stack adjustment, no frame.
mechanics.transfers: none. No CALL, no JMP, no computed transfer, no indirect transfer through a register or a memory operand. The complete 2-instruction listing and the xref export (dependencies.edges = []) agree on zero outgoing transfers.
mechanics.memory: no memory operand of any kind in the complete 2-instruction listing. Therefore no displacement is read and none is written, no field is accessed through any register, and no data-segment address is named. This is what the FIELDS/OFFSETS and GLOBALS checks read, and it is the direct test for in the model test (poisoned receiver snapshot, plus a receiver on a PROT_NONE page).
mechanics.control_flow: none. The complete listing contains no conditional branch, so the body is straight-line with exactly one path and one exit. There is no input that selects a different outcome.
mechanics.stack: the RET carries no immediate and no stack slot is ever read, so zero ordinary stack arguments, zero bytes of callee cleanup, caller owns the stack. Checked behaviourally: the model test pushes a canary before the raw call and requires it to be intact on return.
mechanics.return_word: EAX holds 0x00000202. The MOV is a 5-byte immediate write of 0x00000202, so the upper three bytes of the return register are defined rather than residual -- which is why the return is modelled as a 32-bit word and not a narrower integral or a bool.
mechanics.globals: none. The complete 2-instruction listing names no data-segment address. The record's globals entry says the same: 'The listing names no data-segment address, and the body reaches memory nowhere.'

unresolved_questions: What 0x202 denotes. It is a per-class identifier in an ID space this body never interprets and never computes, and two instructions cannot fix its meaning, its neighbours, or whether the space is dense. The sibling implementations named in the record (0x0096fec0, 0x0097e7d0) obtain their values from a runtime registry, which is consistent with an interned index but confirms nothing here. The reconstruction names the constant for the immediate it is and assigns it no role.

The receiver convention is inferred, not observed. See observed_original_abi.convention_basis. Nothing in the body can corroborate it, which is why the derived ABI record abstained (verdict ABI_UNKNOWN) while the persisted record asserts __thiscall. The model follows the persisted record, and a behavioural test cannot tell the two apart -- a mutation that downgrades the declaration to __cdecl everywhere still passes every runtime assertion. See validation.mutation_check.limitations.

The receiver's type. The decompiler says ILayoutElement *, which is not independently confirmed in a binary with no MSVC RTTI. The model keeps the receiver opaque (void*) and records the disagreement rather than resolving it.

Whether GetProxyID is genuinely virtual in the SDK declaration or a non-virtual method that happens to occupy a slot. Not checkable here: the Spore-ModAPI headers are not present. The machine fact -- a slot at +0x14 of the image at 0x014440d0 -- is not in doubt either way, and the model depends on neither reading.

The extent of the dispatch-table image. Only the eight words actually read are recorded. Whether the image continues past +0x1c, and where it ends, is unresolved; nothing in this body depends on the answer.
Slot +0x18 (0x00980520) has no function record in Ghidra, so the slot immediately after this one is uncharacterised. It is the most likely place a related per-class override would sit.

The slots holding 0x00e31100, 0x00dde980 and 0x00b267f0 in this image were not characterised -- they lie above the low code range and are recorded as opaque words. Whether they are code, data or imported thunks is unresolved and does not affect this body.

reasons.ABI: WARN, and no source file could change it. The machine-derived record's conventions block carries confidence UNKNOWN, which trips the validator's 'the oracle is not proven' arm. The arm above it -- the one that would report the derived record's own ABI_UNKNOWN abstention verbatim, with its recorded reason -- is unreachable for this target, because validate's _abi_category returns the inference as None whenever the pack's `abi` category holds a plain persisted record rather than the inference envelope, and this pack has both. So the surfaced reason is the secondary one. Both say the same thing: the body cannot establish its own convention, and the persisted __thiscall rests on dispatch-word placement alone. This package models the receiver and says so; the WARN is the honest outcome, not a defect to chase.
reasons.CALLS: PASS. The xref export (dependencies.edges = []) and the complete 2-instruction listing each record zero outgoing transfers, and the source span names none. Three independent sides agree on an absence, and an absence is the right thing for this body rather than a gap.
reasons.GLOBALS: PASS. The complete 2-instruction listing names no data-segment address and the span names none. The xref export carries no data-reference edge type to corroborate against, which is not needed for an absence.
reasons.FIELDS/OFFSETS: PASS. The record names no receiver register, so the check claims nothing about the receiver in either direction; and the complete 2-instruction listing was consumed in full by the machine parse (degraded=false, unparsed=0) and contains no memory operand at all, which is the evidence that the body performs no field access. The span declares no field offset, so there is nothing to ground and none is claimed to exist.
reasons.CONSTANTS: PASS, and it is the strong arm rather than the vacuous one. The span states one hexadecimal constant, 0x202, and it appears in the listing. parse.declared_count is 2, equal to the listing length, unparsed 0, degraded false.
reasons.CONTROL FLOW: PASS. The complete 2-instruction listing contains no conditional branch, which is itself the evidence that the body is straight-line. Keyword shape in the source is explicitly not part of this verdict, and the span declares no branch keyword anyway.
reasons.VIRTUAL DISPATCH: PASS. The complete 2-instruction body names no indirect transfer through a register or a memory operand, the machine dispatch record agrees at 0, and the span declares no slot boundary. This is a deliberate modelling choice: the function is reached through a dispatch word, but it performs no dispatch, so writing a slot accessor into the body would assert something the listing refutes. The dispatch-table image lives in the header as observed data and is asserted by the test, not used by the body.
reasons.RETURN SEMANTICS: PASS, and this is where the two packages for this VA differ. The check compares the declared return type as text against the record's abi.return_type. Spelled std::uint32_t, it matches exactly. The prior package returns through its own OpaqueWord alias, which the same check reads as a rename and scores WARN. Both compile to the same machine code; this one is spelled to be comparable. Recorded so the difference is not mistaken for a difference in the reconstruction.
reasons.EVIDENCE COVERAGE: WARN, real and not fixable from this package. 12 of 17 static evidence categories are available. The pack reports unavailable/MISSING for callers_dependencies, callees_dependencies, external_callees, contradictions and semantic_hypotheses, among others. The validator derives this check purely from the pack's categories[*].availability, so no source file, sidecar field or metadata edit can move it. Reported, not chased. The honest ceiling for this target is 0.778, not 1.0.

mutation_check.method: each mutation was applied to a copy of the three package files under /tmp/opencode/mut/, built with the same g++ command, and run; the reconstruction was altered and the model test never was.

results.mutation: M1 -- the immediate at 0x00980510 changed from 0x202 to 0x201
results.detail: twelve assertion failures, all on the return word (0x201 and its decimal 513).

results.mutation: M2 -- the return made receiver-dependent without dereferencing it: `return self != nullptr ? 0x203u : 0x202u;`
results.detail: twelve assertion failures on the return word. The hostile-receiver battery supplies null, 0x00000001, 0xFFFFFFFF and pointer values in turn, so a body whose result varied with the receiver is caught on the first entry that differs.

results.mutation: M3 -- the receiver written at offset +0x10
results.detail: No assertion printed before the crash. The first hostile receiver the model test passes, 0x00000001, is unmapd, so the store faults immediately. The crash is a failure, and it is a less legible one than an assertion: the checks that did the detecting here are the hostile-pointer entries, not the poisoned-receiver byte comparison, which never got to run.

results.mutation: M4 -- the return narrowed to its low byte: `return 0x202u & 0xffu;`
results.detail: twelve assertion failures. This is the check that holds the 32-bit width: the model test asserts the return word equals 0x202, equals 514, has zero upper three bytes, and has sizeof 4, so a 16- or 8-bit model of this return is refuted rather than tolerated.

results.mutation: M5 -- the calling convention downgraded from __thiscall to __cdecl
results.detail: The build fails: the model's own dispatch-slot check assigns the reconstruction's address to ProxyWordFn, a __thiscall function-pointer type, and GCC rejects a __cdecl function pointer there. A coherent variant that downgrades ProxyWordFn to __cdecl as well builds and then passes every runtime assertion (exit 0).

mutation_check.limitations: Stated, not hidden. M5's coherent form passing at runtime is not a defect in the test; it is the truth about this target. The body is byte-identical under __cdecl, __stdcall, __thiscall and __fastcall -- the machine-derived record's own inference C10 says exactly that, and it is why that record reached ABI_UNKNOWN. No behavioural test can distinguish a convention the machine never uses. The convention is therefore carried by placement (the sole DATA reference at 0x014440e4) and by the record, and it is flagged as inferred everywhere it appears. One further blind spot, already noted in the model test's own header: a store that wrote back the value it had just read would leave the poisoned-receiver snapshot identical and so would not be excluded by the byte comparison, though the PROT_NONE-page path would still catch the read half of it.
